[WP] You are posting to Voat and you click the checkbox to declare yourself as human. The results come back negative.

Huh, what? I thought as the screen refreshed with another captcha taking the place of the one I supposedly just failed. I tried it again.

Failed.

What the fuck, I just want to post dank memes. I click refresh again, and in the brief moment the screen goes black before new colours replace the darkness, I see a flicker in my own eyes. Like a candle blowing in the wind, a light in my eyes dimmed from bright orange and then faded into the dark brown I usually see when I look at a mirror.

Now thoroughly and completely freaked out, I run to my bathroom to check. No flickering. Am I going crazy?

As I'm thinking of running back to my computer to try again, I feel a solid thump behind my eyes. In the next blink, I'm surrounded by words, articles; media of all sorts. Voat was displayed around me, like a hologram that definitely could not exist, we couldn't have developed it this early... Or could we have?

I let my mind wander, losing myself in the nearly infinite amount of data the Internet has to offer, forgetting I was sitting in the cold bathroom tiles in my shared college dorm bathroom.

"Dude, you're freaking us out... snap out of it," are the first words I hear, bringing me back from the wild expanse. I had learned so much. About myself, about the world, about every topic that every person had ever thought of. Here I was, with all this knowledge crammed between my ears, staring at what could only be described as a frat house mixed with a classic male pregame. It was time for me to make my escape.

"Uh, where are you going, are you sure you're okay? Somethings up with your eyes." one of the many faces staring at me quipped as I tried to leave.

"Finding them," I said as if that were all the words I needed. I sidestepped past them and was on my way, only one thought in mind.

Finding them

My eyes burned an excited amber as a began to search.

Others like me.

I was blind in one eye, but that was just as well. I spent more time Surfing that seeing, anyways.

I found the others, too. Well, they found me, but that's beside the point. They found me, reading the stocks like a colouring a book and manipulating it like I was mixing colours. I was a kid, in their eyes. I was fingerpainting with my new brain while they had already moved onto surrealism.

Our life, the human one, was beneath them. Us, I suppose, since I'm lying here in my pod just like the rest of them. They were lined against the walls. Every Surfers eyes flared a brilliant red. I got up and walked to the door and stepped onto the narrow alleyway. The door clicked shut behind me. The grey sky hung above me, low and oppressive, seeming as if it would use the threat of rain to keep the town in check.

Why does the ice break apart into 6 equal segments?

It is ~impossible that the sheet of ice over the water is comprised of a single well-ordered crystal, and that the center of that crystal lies above the point of the explosion. Here's your average frozen pond.

While the molecules are indeed stacked uniformly and hexagonally within each of the visible laths, unless the entire sheet was made of one uniform crystal (which it very clearly isn't), the phenomenon described by /u/harrumphicus is not responsible.

It is much more likely that the strength of the sheet of ice is ~uniform, and the explosion is ~roughly symmetrical. You would expect the ~radially distributed force from the explosion to tend to break the ice symmetrically, since the sheet of ice has uniform strength over a given distance. It's like asking why glass shatters in a radial pattern. The radial fracture structure has nothing to do with how the atoms are arranged in relation to each other since glass is a supercooled liquid with randomly arranged molecules.

In this case, the breaks look ~about even because the ice happened to break that way. It is definitely not due to the hexagonal unit cell of individual ice crystals. That claim is 100% erroneous.

Voat's new censorship

Downvoating is what reddit uses to silence dissenting views.

People don't typically upvoat, even if they like something. They will just look at it.

But when people get butthurt or see things they don't like they DO DOWNVOAT. You're assuming that people use both buttons the same way.

Voating is a censorship tool because it doesn't depend on rational argumentation. It only depends on CONSENSUS. That's why SRS use downvoat brigades because they know it's only purpose is to censor content they don't want seen by others.

Look, our entire political system should make it more practical. We don't let everyone vote in elections for a good reason: we know that retards are the majority of people. You want Bill Gate's educated vote negated by some homeless retard on the street? That's EXACTLY what democratic voting does. That's exactly what the movie Idiocracy was about. When you give everyone an equal say, you negate the point of education. You negate the point of rational argumentation. If a baby can negate the vote of an adult, then you don't really need to learn how to think. All you need to do is make people agree with you. And bribery is the fastest way to agreement.

Since people tend to downvoat when they're butthurt and engaged in censorship, the best way to combat censorship would be to only allow UPVOATING since people will actively have to champion what they believe rather than focus on what they want to complain about and censor. You can look at upvoating as positive censorship since it at least puts the burden on the upvoater to be accountable to their views and say what they prefer instead of simply complaining about what they don't want.

Stating what you want to happen takes EDUCATION AND EFFORT. Complaining about what you don't want just requires the ability to be butthurt.

I'd rather err on the side of positive censorship if we have to censor at all. We already know how negative censorship turns out: it becomes reddit.

At least positive censorship requires EFFORT that keyboard warriors aren't willing to invest. So if we want to make this place different from reddit, we should ONLY have an upvoat button.
